Hazard: the owner mutex (and for `store limit' the extent mutex, which every cold read and pool draw needs) is held across link/fsync(file)/fsync(dir)/unlink and feed journal provisioning. A slow or stalled disk blocks every owner quantum (readers, posters, control) and, under E, every extent operation, for the duration of a durable configuration publish. The code comments justify the ordering (durable before the pass reads it; fence before the mutex is released) but the I/O itself need not be inside the mutex: the existing off-mutex job pattern (fnn-owner-batch-job, owner-offlock lane) shows the shape.
fix: Move the publication (stage, link, fsync, directory fsync, unlink) and the feed-journal provisioning out of the section as off-mutex job phases ordered by ACL2 (as the batch job's :extend/:append/:fence phases are, owner.lisp:4579), with only the ACL2 decide and install steps under O; or record a design decision that a live reconfiguration may hold O across its durable publish (then declare the site as an R2 exception in tools/lock_discipline_contracts.json with the justification). Not the checker's to decide.
notes: Not fixed in lane/lock-owner-class; design question, state stays open. Moving the I/O off O needs fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked (admin.lisp:247) split into quanta: (1) stage + authorize-decision under O, (2) fnn-admin-publish (fnn-immutable-publish-effect) and fnn-owner-feed-refresh-configuration's feed-open I/O off O, (3) fn-owner-reconfigure-complete + fnn-owner-refresh-config-cache under O. Nine callers hold the function inside a larger quantum body: admin.lisp:336 (redeem, reply only after durable), :470 (reclaim instant), :600 (store limit, under E with the exact budget reduction after install), :692, auth.lisp:77, bp-control.lisp:107 (drive after release), peer-invite.lisp:142/173/250. Blocking facts: (a) the publish sets *fnn-section-step* (:linked/:replaced, cleared by fnn-fsync-dir) and the section boundary classifies a failure from it (fn-fs-classify); an off-O publish needs ACL2 to name how a failure of phase 2 is classified and fenced (fnn-owner-thread-escape has no step for it); (b) no ACL2 phase model exists for reconfiguration as fn-oqw-phases does for the batch (books/owner-queued-work.lisp); (c) the staged record holds the configuration lock between quanta (fn-psrv-unstage on refusal) and the authorize observation (fnn-lstat of the next name) must be re-validated after the gap.

2026-10-08 lane reconfig-host, HOST STATEMENT (ruling 19; written before the code; host/native/admin.lisp fnn-owner-live-reconfigure, ACL2: books/owner-reconfig-phased.lisp fn-orp-step, keystone fn-orp-step-runs-the-phased-run, and the gate hold books/owner-time-reconfig.lisp). QUANTA. Quantum 1 (the caller's section entry, under O): the caller's prefix, then :stage, :authorize and, for `store limit' only, :reserve under E (the caller's E, which also covers its decision and pool preview); a refusal there unstages and answers. Window A (no O, no E): :observe (lstat of the next generation's name, selecting between the two authorizations ACL2 decided in quantum 1) and :publish (open, write, fsync, link, directory fsync, unlink, close, with its own *fnn-section-step*). Quantum 2 (the same section re-entered as class :commit): by the outcome :complete and :refresh (store cache, newly configured peers), or release/unstage/continue/refuse for a refused publication, or the window's condition re-signalled under O by :fence or :fault with the publication step the window left. Window B (no O): (:feed-io . PEER) per newly configured peer: open, read, pure scan (fn-feed-journal-scan), repair, fsync, lseek. Quantum 3 (re-entered, :commit): (:feed-replay . PEER) applies the scanned entries under O (fn-owner-feed-journal-replay), :install joins the journals to the feeds, :convert under E (the store-limit budget reduction), :continue (the caller's work, run in the quantum that decides the answer), :accept; with no new peer quantum 3 is quantum 2's tail. HELD BETWEEN QUANTA. The staged record (ACL2 refuses a second reconfiguration :busy through fn-ocfg-reconfig-refusal, the stage entry's own reason, and :begin/:take) and the gate's hold: fn-otm-hold-begin in the quantum that leaves for window A, fn-otm-hold-end when the step answered :done (also on the fence/fault unwind); under it fn-otm-hold-next admits only :inspect, :reader and :commit, the committer may not START. WHAT EACH WINDOW OBSERVES. Window A: the filesystem and the values quantum 1 captured (the record, ACL2's two authorizations); no owner state, no O, no E. Window B: the feed directory and the journals of peers no installed feed serves (nothing writes them before :install); no owner state. A concurrent :inspect or :reader quantum sees the owner either before :complete (old configuration, record staged) or after it (new configuration, store cache refreshed in the same quantum, feeds not yet installed). WHY NO HALF-INSTALLED CONFIGURATION IS SEEN. ACL2 installs the new configuration in the one quantum that runs :complete and the store cache follows in that quantum; the feed table changes only at :install in quantum 3; between quantum 2 and quantum 3 the hold admits no quantum that could post, commit, configure or enqueue to a new peer, so the only callers that run see a coherent owner and a feed table that does not yet name the new peers.

scenario: Any live `store reclaim', `store limit' or BP node reconfiguration: the control/BP thread enters the section, publishes the configuration record durably (fsync of file and directory) and opens feed journals while every other thread that needs O (or E) waits. Unprivileged clients are not the trigger (control socket), but a slow disk or a stalled fsync freezes the whole node, including readers, for its duration.
